It's only briefly mentioned in the article but I'm very interested in seeing what happens in the James Risen case. Risen was subpoenaed during an investigation into the CIA's Jeffrey Alexander Sterling by the Bush administration in 2008. Sterling had been a source for Risen in his book State of War, and Risen fought the subpoena, which expired in 2009. However, Sterling was indicted by the Obama administration under the Espionage Act of 1917 in 2010, so the subpoena was renewed. Last summer the Court of Appeals ruled that Risen would have to testify in Sterling's case, and the Supreme Court just rejected his appeal.

Risen has already said that he will still refuse to testify, so if federal prosecutors try to compel his testimony and he ends up in jail the Obama administration will look very, very bad, even to some of the remaining Obama apologists.
